text:
jo: Quick triage — spotted a handful of UI/UX nits in Security > Compliance while prepping a customer demo. Nothing blocking but a few small clarity/a11y/copy things to fix.

carla: share the list, thanks.

jo: 1) Badge ordering/confusion: the small chips in the header currently render as [region] [encryption] which makes the encryption chip feel like a region attribute. Customers interpret this as "Region: eu-west-1, Encryption: true" rather than seeing encryption as a key ownership attribute. Suggest either: move the encryption chip to the left of the region badge, or visually separate it (border + subtle icon) and label it as an ownership token e.g. `Encryption: Customer key (BYOK)` / `Encryption: Redwood key`.

matt: Agree. Also the chip label length matters for mobile narrow states — keep it to ~28 chars max or use a tooltip.

jo: 2) Screen reader semantics: currently SR reads "chip, button" for the encryption token. Propose `aria-label=\"Encryption: customer key (BYOK). Press for key details.\"` and include `aria-describedby` pointing to a hidden text node that explains ownership vs regional storage. Add `role=\"status\"` to the ownership hint when the panel expands so SR users get notified of context changes.

carla: Good call. Also check that the chip has `tabindex=0` and a visible focus indicator.

matt: 3) Focus ring / contrast: the current focus ring is a 1px light grey outline. Needs stronger contrast and size for keyboard nav. Recommendation: use system focus token (4px) or at minimum a 2px solid #0057D9 on white bg to achieve >=3:1.

jo: 4) Region fallback copy: when we fallback to a different region we show a tiny badge "fallback" with no context. Customers ask why retention differs. Proposal: `Region: EU (fallback)` with a tooltip: "Data stored in EU fallback region due to capacity constraints; retention defaults may differ. See Data residency docs." Keep tooltip copy short for translations.

carla: +1. Maybe include a link id for docs so tooltip can deep-link.

matt: 5) Audit log / export semantics: logs are using inconsistent casing and terse event verbs which hurt translation and CSV exports. Example current line: `KEY_ROTATE,alice@example.com,2024-11-02T14:32Z`. Suggest normalized CSV headers and sentence-case events:
```
event_time_utc,event,user_email,details
2024-11-02T14:32:00Z,Key rotated,admin@example.com,Customer key rotated to version v3
```
This makes exports readable and consistent with UI language. Also use `event_time_utc` header explicitly so spreadsheets in different timezones are unambiguous.

aria-bot: accessibility check: ensure the audit table rows have `role=row` and each cell `role=cell` for SRs. Add `aria-sort` if columns are sortable.

jo: 6) Copy suggestions for the encryption token — different wording from existing threads to avoid style collisions: `Encryption: Customer key (BYOK)` or `Encryption: Redwood key`. Keep the short form in the UI but full expansion in a tooltip and accessible label.

matt: 7) Docs/screenshots: once we update text and chips, update the Data residency and KMS docs screenshots to match otherwise docs drift. Small follow-up task for docs.

carla: Good catch on CSV header — are we changing existing exported schema? That could break customers.

jo: We should be conservative: update wording and add header label `event_time_utc` while keeping legacy alias for `time` in the backend for backwards compatibility. Create migration note in release.

ops-bot: Created ticket RDO-731: "Encryption token clarity + audit export header + a11y fixes" (labels: ux, accessibility, compliance).

matt: I'll sketch the chip placement options in Figma and attach a small CSS patch toggle for testing (two branches: left-placement vs separated).

carla: @jo can you draft the tooltip copy and accessibility labels? I'll file the docs update after the final wording.

jo: Will do. Draft tooltip copy: "Data stored in fallback region due to capacity; retention defaults may differ. See data residency docs." — short and linkable.

aria-bot: Once wording lands, I'll run a quick NVDA + VoiceOver pass and report any SR quirks.

matt: Plan: design sketch + PR for chip placement + a11y checklist + CI accessibility checks. Target: small patch in next sprint.

jo: Thanks all — small but important for demos and for enterprise customers. If anyone sees regressions on translations, ping localization.

ops-bot: Linked to epic RDO-700 and added comment: "avoid breaking CSV consumers; keep backend alias for `time` field."
